evidence.note: Shows evaluation itself scales like generation: off-the-shelf reasoning models, simply prompted to generate a chain-of-thought judgment (no evaluator-specific training), improve monotonically with more reasoning tokens and, when made to individually assess every reasoning step rather than a single-pass judgment, a 32B reasoning evaluator beats a specialized 72B PRM by 4.5 F1 points on ProcessBench; folding this into Best-of-N reranking, spending the fixed test-time budget on evaluation-time reasoning (Best-of-8 with a reasoning evaluator) beats spending it on more candidate samples (Best-of-64 with a direct evaluator) by 4.30-6.63 points, and reasoning evaluators are shown to resist reward-model over-optimization that both direct evaluator types suffer from.
evidence.title: Scaling Evaluation-Time Compute with Reasoning Models as Evaluators
